what: The prompt prescribes `python3 -m eval.verify_supported <dir> <op> --output <dir>/verifier_report.json` and then says to READ every loud category from the emitted report. With --output set, main() writes JSON to the file and prints NOTHING to stdout, and returns exit 1 whenever any loud category fired. So the prescribed command produces zero human-readable output plus a bare non-zero exit, which reads as a tool crash.
suggest: Prompt should show the two-step form (run once with --output for the artifact, once without for the text report), or note that --output suppresses stdout and that exit 1 means loud-category-fired, not failure to run.

what: The verifier prompt table lists supported_fail / xpass_drift / xfail_wrong_mode (+ supported_marked_xfail) as the loud categories, but _LOUD_CATEGORIES also contains invalid_unexpected, which drives the CLI exit code. My run had all four prompt-named categories at 0 and still exited 1 on invalid_unexpected=2, with no guidance on how to triage or route it (it turned out to be a feature_spec/test_translated harness artifact, not an op defect).
suggest: Add an invalid_unexpected row to the prompt category table: what it means (a cell matching INVALID that ran anyway), that it is usually a harness/feature_spec authoring issue rather than an op bug, and that it must be reported in the INVALID audit rather than fixed op-side.

what: The InitUninitMode doc says only: when calling tilize() multiple times back-to-back you can skip redundant init/uninit (InitOnly/Neither/UninitOnly). My gamma-ingest loop met that stated precondition exactly (N consecutive tilize calls, nothing between them, identical template params), and the amortized form is SILENTLY WRONG: every chunk after the first is corrupted (PCC 0.24 / -0.018 / 0.0035 on three shapes). The real precondition appears to be stronger - the calls must also share one CB reserve/push group on the OUTPUT CB - and it is not documented anywhere.
suggest: State the actual precondition next to the enum: back-to-back is not sufficient; the calls must not interleave separate cb_reserve_back/cb_push_back groups on the output CB (or whatever the true invariant is), and note that violating it corrupts output silently rather than hanging.

what: The golden suite for this op is ~40.8k cells and takes ~25 minutes wall-clock, but the Bash tool caps a foreground command at 600000 ms (10 min). The prescribed foreground invocation is therefore killed mid-run every time; I lost one full 10-minute run before switching to nohup setsid + polling. Any op with a large cartesian will hit this.
suggest: Prompt should tell the verifier up front to launch eval_test_runner.sh detached (nohup setsid ... > log) and poll the log/results dir, and note that a killed run leaves /tmp/tt-device.dirty set so the next run self-resets.

what: The Build Environment section says to run ./build_metal.sh, but in an eval tree with nuked ops that target ALWAYS fails: the cmake cache has TTNN_BUILD_TESTS=ON/TT_METAL_BUILD_TESTS=ON and the gtest sources still include headers of the removed ops (test_graph_basic.cpp -> normalization/softmax/softmax.hpp, test_conv2d.cpp -> conv/conv2d/conv2d.hpp). ninja stops before _ttnn.so links, so the tree looks unbuildable. The implementer had hit the same wall (it is noted in changelog.md).
suggest: Prompt should say: if build_metal.sh fails only in tests/ targets, reconfigure with -DTTNN_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DTT_METAL_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DTT_UMD_BUILD_TESTS=OFF and rebuild; the library targets are what the golden suite needs.
